title.value: Considerations and Recommendations from the ISMRM Diffusion Study Group for preclinical diffusion MRI: Part 1 — In vivo small-animal imaging
title.justification: The paper's focus is explicitly stated in the title, highlighting the ISMRM Diffusion Study Group's recommendations and considerations for preclinical diffusion MRI, particularly for in vivo small-animal imaging.
title.quote: Considerations and Recommendations from the ISMRM Diffusion Study Group for preclinical diffusion MRI: Part 1 — In vivo small-animal imaging

analysis.description: This paper provides recommendations from the ISMRM Diffusion Study Group on best practices for preclinical diffusion MRI focusing on in vivo small-animal imaging. It discusses general considerations for designing experiments, including species differences, acquisition protocols, data processing, and the importance of responsible and reproducible research.

type.justification: The paper presents empirical guidelines and recommendations based on practical experiences and evidence from the preclinical diffusion MRI community. It is not theoretical but rather grounded in practice.
type.quote: This work aims to present selected recommendations and guidelines from the diffusion community, on best practices for preclinical dMRI of in vivo animals.

name.justification: The paper extensively discusses the use of diffusion MRI, which is a critical technique in neuroimaging, for examining microstructural brain properties in small animal models.
name.quote: Diffusion MRI (dMRI) is a non-invasive technique that exploits the hindered or restricted diffusion of water molecules in biological tissue to extract information about tissue microstructure in both normal and abnormal states.

name.justification: The paper focuses on imaging techniques and considerations specifically for preclinical studies, particularly involving small animals.
name.quote: This work aims to present selected recommendations and guidelines from the diffusion community, on best practices for preclinical dMRI of in vivo animals.

name.justification: The paper mentions the use of multi-compartment biophysical models, particularly for analyzing small animal diffusion MRI data.
name.quote: Given recent advances in acquisition efficiency and speed, we advocate a minimal acquisition of two-shell data leading to DKI analysis as the new “default” over simple DTI derived from single-shell data. A two-shell acquisition also opens up data analysis possibilities beyond DKI, e.g. for multi-compartment biophysical models.

is_contributed.justification: The paper does not claim to contribute this model; it is mentioned as part of existing practices in diffusion MRI analysis.
is_contributed.quote: A two-shell acquisition also opens up data analysis possibilities beyond DKI, e.g. for multi-compartment biophysical models.

is_executed.justification: The paper discusses the model's use in theoretical frameworks for planning experiments and analysis, not in execution on processors like GPU or CPU.
is_executed.quote: The 'optimal' q-t coverage is highly dependent on the microstructure feature one wishes to maximize sensitivity to...A two-shell acquisition also opens up data analysis possibilities beyond DKI, e.g., for multi-compartment biophysical models.

is_compared.justification: The paper does not provide numerical comparison or specific performance metrics comparing multi-compartment biophysical models to other models.
is_compared.quote: Given recent advances in acquisition efficiency and speed, we advocate a minimal acquisition of two-shell data leading to DKI analysis as the new 'default' over simple DTI derived from single-shell data.
